Craft — the process

Listen. Structure.
Draft. Disappear.

Every voice has a grammar. Before a word goes on the page we learn yours — the phrases you reach for, the stories you retell, the jokes you time badly and the ones you land. The finished manuscript should read like you on your best month, not like us on any day.

i.

Listen

Eight to twenty hours of recorded conversation. We interview the way biographers do — sideways, patiently, twice. The transcript becomes the quarry every chapter is cut from.

ii.

Structure

An argument-first outline you can defend in a boardroom: what the book claims, chapter by chapter, and why a stranger should care by page two. Nothing is drafted until the skeleton stands on its own.

iii.

Draft

Chapters arrive in your voice, on schedule, with margins full of questions only you can answer. Two structured revision rounds; unlimited honesty.

iv.

Disappear

Files transferred, drafts destroyed, NDA outliving the engagement. At launch we are strangers who happen to have read your book early — and loved it, obviously.
